fleetHours.note: No cumulative total has been published. `fleet:hours` is built and measured (orchestrator, lead/fleet-hours) and reports 54.11 worker-hours across every capture on disk -- which spans several runs and protocol versions and is therefore NOT any single run's figure, which is why no edition carries it yet. Until an entry names one finished run, the report prints 'not instrumented' in those words.
fleetHours.//: A FLEET-HOURS ENTRY MUST NAME THE RUN IT WAS COMPUTED FROM **AND** THAT RUN'S finishedAt. The report REFUSES a total missing either, rather than printing it with a caveat -- a footnote is something a reader skips, and unlike a convention a refusal cannot be satisfied by remembering. `runFinishedAt` was added 2026-09-06 on orchestrator's suggestion after a total named a run still in flight: a NAMED but UNFINISHED run makes the field fillable and FALSE, which is harder to catch than a missing one. Shape (the placeholder values below are deliberately not plausible numbers -- an example that reads like data gets copied): {"total": "<HH h MM m, from the instrument, never typed>", "run": "<unit + InvocationID + case count + protocol>", "runFinishedAt": "<ISO 8601, the run's own finish, not when you recorded it>", "reportedBy": "orchestrator", "at": "<ISO 8601>", "method": "sum of each capture's last cumulative diagnostics.atMs -- never wall clock x worker count"}. Delete the `status` key when adding these. THE METHOD IS NOT NEGOTIABLE AND AN EARLIER VERSION OF IT WAS IMPOSSIBLE: this field read 'sum of per-case startedAt..finishedAt from the run's progress file' until orchestrator measured that no such data exists -- 0 of 1,623 cases carry any time field, because only the transient `current` array holds startedAt and an entry leaves it the moment the case completes. The timings a finished run needs are exactly the ones that file has discarded. Same shape as this repo's waiter polling for a `p.captured` that was never a field. The cost lives in each capture's own diagnostics, where bench-capture has read it all along. WHAT THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES, so an edition can caveat it accurately: capture OCCUPANCY only -- not idle time between dispatches, not provisioning, reboots or power. It refuses rather than printing 0.00 when it billed nothing, and distinguishes 'no JSON found' from 'walked N and billed none'. THE `method` STRING IS TO BE COPIED FROM THE INSTRUMENT, NEVER RETYPED. `fleet:hours --json` is gaining a `method` field for exactly this reason (orchestrator, agreed 2026-09-06): the same fact currently lives in CLAUDE.md's `fleet:hours` row AND here, with nothing comparing them, which is this repo's most-repeated defect arriving in the two files that exist to stop people getting this number wrong. The remedy is the one this repo prefers -- delete a copy rather than pin two -- so once that field exists, paste it from the tool's own output and this string is produced by the thing it describes. Until then the string below is correct and was itself a correction: it read 'sum of per-case startedAt..finishedAt from the run's progress file' until orchestrator measured that no such data exists (0 of 1,623 cases carry any time field).

gates_//: Shape of a `gates` entry: {"command": "npm run lab:job -- -e job=rules-real-pages", "reportedBy": "orchestrator", "at": "<ISO 8601>", "output": "<the gate's OWN text, verbatim, not a summary>"}. The newest entry by `at` is the one printed. Older than `staleAfterHours` still prints, marked STALE and saying it describes an earlier state of the corpus -- an absent line and an old line mean different things and must never render the same.
achievements_//: SECTION 3 OF THE BOARD DOCUMENT: what the product can now DO or PROVE that it could not before -- never commit counts, which measure activity rather than capability. This is the one section no API can derive, so it is authored, and every entry carries the EVIDENCE that makes it a capability claim rather than an assertion. An empty list prints as 'nothing recorded for this window' with what that means, never as a gap the reader has to notice. Shape: {"claim": "<what the product can now do or prove, in a sentence a non-engineer reads>", "evidence": "<the command, the artefact or the measurement that shows it>", "issue": <number or null>, "reportedBy": "<agent>", "at": "<ISO 8601>"}. AN ENTRY WHOSE `evidence` IS ANOTHER AGENT'S SUMMARY IS NOT EVIDENCE. Point at what printed it. `boardClaim` IS WHAT THE BOARD READS and `claim` is what the engineers do. Sections one to five of the board document carry no repository internals at all -- no file names, no identifiers, no command names -- so a claim written for a colleague cannot appear there. The evidence and the exact references stay in the appendix. Added 2026-09-06 on board feedback: every internal reference in edition 1 told them the product manager was pointing at files instead of managing the product. AND THE EVIDENCE BLOCK OPENS WITH WORDS AND ENDS WITH IDENTIFIERS, IN PARENTHESES. Board feedback on edition 2: the body had been cleaned of internals and the appendix was still LEADING with them, which teaches the reader the habit is only hidden. Plain sentence first, exact reference last, so anyone who wants to check can and nobody else has to read past it.

achievements.claim: What is open now survives the loss of this machine.
achievements.evidence: The list of open work, its acceptance criteria and its release blockers now lives in a hosted issue tracker rather than in a document on one machine. Verified by listing the issues and the release milestone directly from the tracker. Previously the answer lived in a 1,049-line file that contradicted itself, and five items checked during the move were already finished. (GitHub Issues and milestones on DanBeckDev/a11y-witness; the contradiction is tracked as issue #19.)
achievements.boardClaim: The list of what is open now survives the loss of the one machine this project runs on.

achievements.claim: The project can say what a capture costs in worker time, for the first time.
achievements.evidence: A tool now exists that adds up how long each recorded page occupied a capture machine, so the fleet's cost can be stated rather than guessed. It reports 54.11 machine-hours across 5,395 of the 5,396 recordings it found, with a middle value of 27.4 seconds per page. The figure is summed per recording from each recording's own timings, never from elapsed time multiplied by the number of machines. (`fleet:hours`, built by orchestrator on branch `lead/fleet-hours`, commit `10ad2e5`; tracked as issue #21.)
achievements.boardClaim: We can say for the first time how much machine time it costs to record a page with a screen reader.

achievements.claim: The page written to prove a rule was recorded, and did not prove it.
achievements.evidence: A rule could previously only be demonstrated on pages we wrote ourselves, which cannot falsify the assumptions behind it. A page exercising it was written and has now been recorded — and the recording showed the opposite of what was expected. The conformant version was measured correctly and the FAILING version was not, because the same property that makes a page fail this rule also prevents the tool from observing it. The tool now reports 'cannot say' on those pages instead of reporting them as clean, and the underlying fix is scheduled. Superseded issue #2, now tracked as #76. (`focus-panel-undismissable-help` in `packages/lab/src/training/real-page-corpus.mjs`; measured 2026-09-06 by orchestrator on both halves of the pair, same fleet, minutes apart.)
achievements.boardClaim: A page built to prove a rule showed instead that the rule cannot see that fault.

achievements.claim: Two capture defects that would have silently mismeasured real pages are fixed and awaiting merge.
achievements.evidence: Two faults were found that would have made the tool measure a different web page from the one it was asked to examine, in both cases without any error being raised. Both are fixed and both are waiting to be merged, so nothing in production has changed yet. They were found by checking which parts of the code unmerged work already touches, rather than by reading the code. (Branch `agent/route-change-order-and-dialog-restore`; tracked as issue #16.)
achievements.boardClaim: We found and fixed two recording faults that would have silently measured the wrong web page.

achievements.claim: The corpus survives losing its machine.
achievements.evidence: Several thousand screen-reader recordings, which cannot be re-recorded once a browser updates, existed in exactly one place. A copy now sits off that machine, and it was checked by downloading it back and counting what was inside rather than by trusting that the upload succeeded. 7,694 files, 108.1 MB of evidence in an 8.5 MB archive, zero empty files. Each step of the chain distrusts the one before it: the machine holding the corpus verifies its own archive against what is on its disk, the transfer is counted on arrival, and the upload is verified by retrieval. (`corpus:snapshot` -> `lab:fetch -e artifact=corpus-archive` -> `corpus:release`, orchestrator, 2026-09-06; release tag corpus-2026-09-06_19-31-35; tracked as issue #43.)
achievements.boardClaim: The recordings this product rests on now exist in more than one place.

capacity.note: Engineering capacity waiting for its next assignment is not yet instrumented and will print as those words until a week of data exists. It is derived from LABEL EVENTS, which are timestamped: a `session:*` label and `in-progress` are applied together when a row is briefed, so the gap between one session's `in-progress` being removed and that same session's next `in-progress` being added is the measure.
capacity.//: WHY NOT THE ASSIGNEE, which was the first design: this repository has TWO assignable accounts and NINE sessions -- every agent operates as the same GitHub user. The assignee can record assigned-versus-unassigned and cannot record WHICH session, so a week of it would have answered correctly about the wrong thing. Caught by dispatcher before the first day of data rather than after the first week. A per-session LABEL carries attribution and timing in one mechanism, which also removes the second source of truth the first design needed.

definitionChanges.what: The worker rule changed from pull-AFTER-report to pull-BEFORE-report: a finishing session now takes its next row and reports both in one message.
definitionChanges.effect: The measured gap becomes structurally small from this point. A series spanning this change will show an improvement that is a DEFINITION CHANGE, not a change in how long anyone waited. Any chart or figure crossing it must mark it.

capacity_//: SECTION 5 PRINTS THIS. An entry with `status: not instrumented` prints those words; a real total must name the window it covers AND carry any definitionChanges that fall inside it -- a measure whose definition moved mid-series is two measures wearing one name, which is this project's most-repeated defect with a clock attached.
